PE->PAISES BAJOS.note: corridor default; asparagus pair overrides to HIGH

PE->ISRAEL.note: AIR-dominant lane (95.7% observed). Cold treatment required at origin (phyto). Air transit + hub transshipment = high cold-chain break risk. Ocean 35d rule not the primary driver — air+cold-treatment stack is.

G1|ISRAEL.reason_short: AC-confirmed 2026-07-09. AIR-dominant + cold treatment required at origin: extra cost/delay pre-shipment PLUS near-certain cold-chain break at air hub during transshipment. The cold-treatment investment at origin is undermined mid-transit — high spoilage/reject probability + thin resale market on rejection.

G1|ALEMANIA.reason_short: AC-confirmed. Ocean 19-22d eats shelf life; strict quality culture; hard to re-place rejects. Overrides Rotterdam Low.

G1|ESPAÑA.reason_short: Asparagus benefits from air-dominant + deep resale (Mercamadrid). Applies best to asparagus specifically.

G1|ESTADOS UNIDOS.reason_short: Short transit + deep market; fruit-fly protocol compliance is binding

G1|TAILANDIA.reason_short: Long transit near CA ceiling; moderate resale depth

G2|EU.reason_short: Robust demand + ripening infra; DM/maturity claims are main friction

G3|COLOMBIA.reason_short: TM-2026-012 lane: short transit but thin market depth + first-time counterparties

G3|ESTADOS UNIDOS.reason_short: Cold-treatment protocol mandatory; protocol certification gates the deal

G4|EU.reason_short: Physically low-risk; EUDR DDS is the gating item

GX|EGIPTO.reason_short: Long transshipped transit + customs variability + payment-rail friction (fresh only)

GX|JORDANIA.reason_short: Long transshipped transit + customs variability + payment-rail friction (fresh only)

rules.air_cold_treatment_stack_note: Independent rule from the 35d ocean rule. A corridor whose predominant transport is AIR AND requires cold treatment at origin for the commodity has near-certain cold-chain break during air-hub transshipment. Floors the C4 flag at HIGH for perishables (G1-G3 fresh) regardless of ocean transit norms.
